title: From Transcription to Live Music: Gemini's Audio Stack — Thor Schaeff, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: A Google DeepMind developer-advocate talk demoing Gemini's audio stack: audio understanding/transcription with structured outputs, controllable TTS via 'director's notes', a real-time speech-to-speech model, and Lyra music generation. It is almost entirely product marketing and demos, with only a couple of transferable engineering practices.

takeaways.technique: Published coding-agent skills for tricky APIs
takeaways.what_they_do: They ship 'agent skills' (installable guidance files) for their APIs, explicitly because real-time audio is hard and the skills 'steer' coding agents to correct usage.

takeaways.technique: One structured-output call instead of a pipeline
takeaways.what_they_do: A single request with a response schema returns speakers, timestamps, language, translation, emotion and summary together, replacing a multi-step cascade.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this was one API call uh to Gemini 3 Flash preview ... I just gave it a response schema so kind of structured outputs

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of picking from a huge preset library, they keep ~30 base voices and steer behavior with an explicit 'audio profile / scene / director's note' prompt structure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're setting the scene, we're instructing sort of this director's note ... just like how you would direct a human
